### Geography role, aligned pairs

Role class agreement **45 / 50**. 3-role: each reader's geography role is put in a class (climrr.wp4adj.ROLE_CLASS_OF, climrr.wp4_judgements.ROLE_CLASS_OF_R1); same class -> agree; different -> the more conservative class in the order ['unknown', 'citation_or_person', 'affiliation', 'other', 'data_source', 'contextual', 'cited_study_area', 'study_area']; geography adopted unknown -> role unknown. A role disagreement makes the pair adjudicated_modified.

| Claim | Reader 1 role [class] | Reader 2 role [class] | Adopted class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LIT2-000203-C1 | study area of the cited study [cited_study_area] | contextual mention [contextual] | **contextual** |
| LIT2-000673-C2 | evaluation site (fire source region) [study_area] | data source [data_source] | **data_source** |
| LIT2-000786-C1 | regions of the reviewed studies [cited_study_area] | data source [data_source] | **data_source** |
| LIT2-000786-C3 | study area of the cited study [cited_study_area] | contextual mention [contextual] | **contextual** |
| LIT2-000927-C4 | target of the recommendation [other] | study area [study_area] | **other** |

### Single-reader claims

- reader-1-only **LIT2-000084-C4** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): In the Southern Great Plains, heat wave frequency, duration and intensity rose gradually as irrigation amount or irrigated area declined.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000084-C5** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): The most affected areas are in Texas, Kansas, Nebraska and California, where irrigated area is greatest; nearly 35 million people live in counties sensitive to heat wave increases with irrigation decline.
- reader-2-only **154971876-c4** → `LIT2-000084-B4` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): The authors state the Southern High Plains are most likely to suffer more and longer heat waves if irrigation is reduced due to groundwater depletion.
- reader-2-only **154971876-c5** → `LIT2-000084-B5` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): Nearly 35 million people live in counties sensitive to heat wave increases with irrigation decline, mostly in California and Texas.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000185-C2** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): For Portugal, the magnitude of burnt area agrees strongly across the three sources compared (GlobFire, EFFIS remote sensing and national reports).; **the blind reader had considered and not promoted this passage**
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000185-C5** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): Fire danger indicators such as the Canadian Fire Weather Index have recently shown the highest values of the last 37 years in many European countries.; **the blind reader had considered and not promoted this passage**
- reader-2-only **208499235-c4** → `LIT2-000185-B4` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): A cited assessment in Mato Grosso compared an early GlobFire version with the TREES product and found similar polygon-area distributions (9% total burnt-area difference), with a significant 21% difference only for smaller polygons.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000203-C3** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): A cited study showed low-income countries will bear a greater burden of severe heat events than high-income countries, even if warming targets below 1.5 °C are met.; **the blind reader had considered and not promoted this passage**
- reader-2-only **211267687-c3** → `LIT2-000203-B3` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): Citing prior Gambian studies, the paper states women work between 50% and 83% of a 9-hour day on agricultural work, depending on season, even when pregnant.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000315-C2** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): In central North America's Mississippi valley, irrigation produced significant increases of 0.3-0.5 °C in the 50th, 90th and 99th percentile wet-bulb temperatures, with no change in median temperature.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000315-C5** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): A cited regional modelling study of California and Nebraska found mean heat index decreased less than mean temperature in irrigated areas, and peak heat index, unlike peak temperature, did not decrease under irrigation.
- reader-2-only **225397451-c3** → `LIT2-000315-B3` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): In the Ganges valley, irrigation weakened summer monsoon flow, increasing surface solar flux and decreasing cloudiness, with no significant humidity increase; this region saw wet-bulb temperature decrease.
- reader-2-only **225397451-c5** → `LIT2-000315-B5` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): Citing prior work, the paper states large-scale wet-bulb temperature currently peaks at about 31°C during heat waves in densely populated areas such as northern India and around the Persian Gulf.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000366-C2** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): On the forest fire data set, the optimized framework's classification accuracy is not lower than that of general classifiers (SVM, random forest), and it shows natural regional adaptability.
- reader-2-only **229495849-c3** → `LIT2-000366-B3` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): The authors conclude that their framework can effectively predict the occurrence of forest fires based on meteorological data and has good regional adaptability.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000470-C1** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): After two rounds of Delphi scoring, the 59 originally developed recommendations were reduced to 40 occupational heat safety recommendations across eight topics.; **the blind reader had considered and not promoted this passage**
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000470-C5** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): California, Washington and Minnesota are the only three US states that enforce OSHA-approved heat safety standards.
- reader-2-only **237371886-c4** → `LIT2-000470-B4` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): Citing McCarthy et al. (2019), after a Central Texas municipality's heat-illness prevention program, heat-related illnesses decreased over 9 years and workers' compensation costs per illness fell by an average of 50%.
- reader-2-only **237371886-c5** → `LIT2-000470-B5` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): Citing prior studies, the paper states the majority of worker heat-related fatalities occurred during the first week of work and at worksites without a heat acclimatization policy.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000499-C4** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): In the worst-case situation defined by the model (forest under 10 m to the west, undefended, facing west-south-west, dense vegetation), 71% of houses were impacted, versus 3% in the best case.; **the blind reader had considered and not promoted this passage**
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000499-C5** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): Preparedness actions and response actions were the most important themes for house impact, more important than house construction, landscape fuels, topography and weather.
- reader-2-only **238725720-c3** → `LIT2-000499-B3` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): Burnt houses closer than 40 m increased the likelihood of a house being impacted by approximately 10%, which the authors suggest reflects house-to-house transmission, with caution about spatial clustering.
- reader-2-only **238725720-c5** → `LIT2-000499-B5` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): The authors conclude that maintaining defensible space, which involves reducing multiple sources of wildfire fuel around the house, is the most important message.
- reader-2-only **244714495-c2** → `LIT2-000560-B2` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): The authors suggest the proposed model's better performance could come from the dynamic auto-encoder's ability to estimate for confounding factors.
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000662-C4** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): Urban expansion outpaced green expansion in the 49 cities: the mean annual GEII was 0.017% against a mean UEII of 1.5%.; **the blind reader had considered and not promoted this passage**
- reader-1-only **LIT2-000662-C5** (tier C, `not_independently_found`): A cited study found 2000-2010 heat-related worker fatality rates of 0.37, 0.33 and 0.24 per million workers per year in Florida, Texas and California, among the top ten states.; **the blind reader had considered and not promoted this passage**
- reader-2-only **250039675-c2** → `LIT2-000662-B2` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): Heat wave duration change was negatively correlated with UEII, which the authors read as cities expanding more rapidly might receive fewer consecutive heat wave days.
- reader-2-only **250039675-c5** → `LIT2-000662-B5` (tier C, `blind_reader_only`): The authors state results imply cities would be better in a more compact pattern with more expanded green areas to mitigate negative health impacts of heat waves.; **reader 1 had considered and not promoted this passage**
